subject: unexpected money

hook.say: You get ten thousand dollars you didn't plan for. There are four reactions, and they're all about what you think you deserve.

types.name: The Spender
types.say: It's already spent before it lands. That was the point of it.

types.name: The Saver
types.say: It goes somewhere safe and you never think about it again.

types.name: The Investor
types.say: You ask what it could become in five years.

types.name: The Avoider
types.say: You leave it sitting there, because deciding feels dangerous.

kicker.say: A windfall doesn't change your money habits. It just makes them louder.

caption: Nobody thinks they'd be the spender until the money is actually in the account.

subject: money personalities

hook.say: There are four money personalities. None of them are about how much you earn.

types.name: The Optimizer
types.say: You'll spend an hour to save four dollars, and genuinely enjoy it.
types.tag: an hour to save four dollars

types.name: The Status Buyer
types.say: You buy the version people can see.

types.name: The Quiet Saver
types.say: Nobody knows your number. That's the whole point.

types.name: The Avoider
types.say: You'd rather not look. Looking makes it real.

kicker.say: Your spending is a story about safety. Read it before you judge it.

caption: The status buyer and the quiet saver are usually the same person, ten years apart.

subject: how you save

hook.say: Everyone saves differently. Only one of these actually works.

types.name: The Automatic
types.say: It leaves before you see it. You never miss it.

types.name: The Manual
types.say: You transfer what's left at the end of the month. There's never anything left.

types.name: The Round-Up
types.say: Small amounts, constantly. It feels like nothing and quietly becomes something.

types.name: The Never
types.say: There's always a reason this month is different.

kicker.say: Saving isn't discipline. It's a system that runs without you.

caption: If your savings depend on remembering, you don't have savings. You have intentions.

subject: tracking money

hook.say: How you track your money tells you more than your bank balance does.

types.name: The App
types.say: Three apps, two budgets, one graph you check every morning.

types.name: The Spreadsheet
types.say: Six tabs, colour coded, updated every Sunday night.

types.name: The Head
types.say: You know roughly. Roughly is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

types.name: The None
types.say: You find out at the end of the month, usually standing in a shop.
types.tag: end of month, in a shop

kicker.say: You can't fix what you refuse to look at. Ten minutes a week is enough.

caption: The spreadsheet person and the no-tracker person often have the same amount of money. One just sleeps better.

subject: money stress

hook.say: Money stress shows up in four ways. Only one of them actually helps.

types.name: The Budget
types.say: You make a plan at midnight and feel briefly in control.

types.name: The Avoid
types.say: You don't open the app. If you don't see it, it's a rumour.

types.name: The Earn
types.say: You take on more work instead of looking at the numbers.

types.name: The Deny
types.say: You buy something small to feel better about the thing you can't afford.

kicker.say: Financial stress is usually a math problem wrapped in a shame problem.

caption: Avoidance is the most expensive money habit there is. It charges interest.

subject: buying when sad

hook.say: There are four things people buy when they're sad. None of them fix it.

types.name: The Comfort
types.say: Food, a blanket, something warm. You're not buying a thing, you're buying care.

types.name: The Upgrade
types.say: A better version of something you already own and already liked.

types.name: The Impulse
types.say: You don't remember deciding. It arrives on Thursday.

types.name: The Nothing
types.say: You want to. You just can't justify it. So you buy nothing and feel worse.

kicker.say: Retail therapy works for about eleven minutes. Then it's just a receipt.

caption: The purchase isn't the problem. The feeling you were trying to skip is.
